model.projection: polar stereographic, sphere R = 1737.4 km, true scale at the pole, centre 90S 0E

assumptions: Input latitude is planetocentric and longitude east-positive in the DEM's body-fixed frame (synthetic (no lunar frame)); no frame conversion is applied.

Zone = DEM pixels whose centre (exact inverse polar stereographic) lies within radius_m great-circle distance of the zone centre on the 1737.4 km reference sphere; terrain height is ignored for selection.

Per-pixel slope: Horn (1981) 3x3 finite differences on the native 20 m grid, ground spacing = map_scale / k * (R + h) / R with k = 1 + (rho / 2R)^2 (services/science/src/slope_core.hpp, identical to the web slope tiles at level 0).
Slope is measured from the reference-sphere radial direction, not the local gravity (geoid) normal.

No-data: non-finite or |h| > 100 km heights, or any no-data in the 3x3 window; never treated as flat. Every zone pixel must have a full 3x3 window inside the grid and lie south of the label's MAXIMUM_LATITUDE, else status = out_of_coverage.

fraction_ok = valid pixels with slope <= max_slope_deg / valid pixels. verdict = insufficient_data if nodata_count / pixel_count > max_nodata_fraction (or no valid pixel), else pass iff fraction_ok >= required_fraction, else fail.
slope_p95_deg is the nearest-rank 95th percentile of valid pixel slopes; worst_pixel is the steepest valid pixel (first in raster order on ties).
warnings: SYNTHETIC DEM: this result comes from a test grid, not from lunar data.

Slope at the DEM's 20 m grid (Horn window ~60 m) is NOT lander-footprint slope: boulders, small craters and roughness below the DEM resolution are invisible, and slopes at lander scale are generally steeper. A pass is a DEM-scale screening result, not a validated or certified landing site.
